title: Diagnostic: Overlapping inout Access

docs.title: Memory Safety — Conflicting Access to In-Out Parameters

hints: Swift forbids two simultaneous write accesses to the same variable.
Pass the **same** variable as both `inout` arguments.
jsBridge: The **law of exclusivity**: while an `inout` access is in progress, nothing else may access that variable. JS has no such rule. Swift enforces it at compile time where it can and at runtime otherwise, which prevents a class of aliasing bugs.

compass.q: Can a JS function receive the same object twice and get confused by aliasing? What does Swift prevent?
Runtime exclusivity violations: when does the compiler defer to a runtime check (class properties, globals)?
Have you seen "Simultaneous accesses to 0x…, but modification requires exclusive access" in a crash? What caused it?
